title: Carrying soup across a sticky floor

data.source: Salamon and Berry (1983); Sivak and Crooks (2012); Benamou and Brenier (2000); Aurell, Mejia-Monasterio and Muratore-Ginanneschi (2011); Schmiedl and Seifert (2007). Computed, with one seeded simulation of a trapped particle.

prediction: R6 is the thermodynamic-length bound made weaker: the tight bound uses the square root of the friction as its ruler and is met by even pacing in that ruler; zeta is friction, tied to the Fisher metric only through a physical relaxation time; and the length is the system's own travel, not the dial's.
baseline: Thermodynamic length (Salamon and Berry 1983; Sivak and Crooks 2012) and the optimal-transport bound (Benamou and Brenier 2000; Aurell et al. 2011).
why: R6 held on every path and was never tight: the real floor was the squared length measured with the square root of the friction, and R6's number sat well below it. zeta turned out to be plain friction, equal to kT times a relaxation time times the Fisher metric in the one case tried, so information geometry alone cannot give it. Read with the dial's travel instead of the particle's, the bound would have been broken by the known best protocol. Phoenix already records R6 as a RESULT that is "existing thermodynamic-length mathematics"; this check agrees.
